ai.description: This 4–6 cm frog is lime-green to brownish with a white belly. It features two black spots behind the eyes and extensive webbing between the fingers and toes for gliding. Family: Rhacophoridae.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Rhacophorus bipunctatus* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, small black spot at the base of each finger and toe, which is absent in similar species.
ai.habitat: This species inhabits evergreen and semi-evergreen forests in the Himalayas, typically found near water bodies at elevations ranging from 500 to 2,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Himalaya Flying Frog is primarily nocturnal, using its large, webbed feet to glide between trees to forage for insects and escape predators.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Rhacophorus bipunctatus* breeds during the monsoon, laying clutches of 30–60 eggs in foam nests attached to vegetation overhanging water bodies.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Himalaya Flying Frog occurs in Northeast India, specifically in Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, and Tripura, at 200–2,000m elevation.
ai.callDescription: The Himalaya Flying Frog produces a series of rapid, high-pitched "tink-tink-tink" notes, typically heard from vegetation near forest pools or streams.
